usageNotes: Use this to enable, disable, or tune the per-VM firewall — including default policies, DHCP/NDP passthrough, IP filtering, and traffic log levels. The VM's firewall must first be enabled at the node/cluster level for these settings to take effect. Requires VM.Config.Network on the VM path; returns null synchronously (no UPID — the change is applied immediately).

examples.summary: Enable the firewall with DROP default policies, enable DHCP passthrough, and log inbound warnings

tips: The `enable` flag controls whether the VM-level firewall is active at all — rules exist but are unenforced when false.
Enabling `ipfilter` without any ipfilter-net<id> ipsets implicitly applies sane anti-spoofing defaults per interface; for containers it also whitelists configured IP addresses.
Use the `delete` param (comma-separated config key names) to revert specific options to their defaults rather than hard-coding the default value, which avoids drift if upstream defaults change.
Pass `digest` (retrieved from the GET counterpart) to guard against concurrent edits overwriting each other.
Changing `policy_in` to DROP is a common lockout risk — ensure at least one ACCEPT rule for SSH/management exists before applying.
